::: {.callout-warning}
## Working draft: verify before classroom use

This directory was assembled from a broad initial online research pass. It has **not** received complete editorial, technical, licensing, accessibility, age-suitability, or classroom review. Entries are leads, not endorsements. Descriptions may be incomplete, access conditions may change, and important limitations may be missing. A teacher must open and assess each resource before assigning it, and students must verify every claim, file, dimension, licence, and machine setting they use.
:::

Use these working notes to find ideas, learn a process, inspect how something works, or locate material that may support an original design after verification. The strongest links also appear inside the lessons where students need them.

**Last reviewed: October 5, 2026.** Websites, prices, account rules, and licences change. Confirm the current terms before classroom use.

::: {.callout-important}
## Free access is not the same as permission to copy

A page that is free to view may contain paid files, copyrighted photographs, restricted trademarks, or models with different licences. For every reused asset, record the **creator, page title, URL, access date, and licence**. Check whether attribution, adaptation, redistribution, or commercial use is allowed. Measure and test downloaded geometry before fabrication. A community upload is not proof that dimensions, safety, ownership, or printability are correct.
:::

## How the access labels work

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Open source / open content** | Source or content is available under a stated open licence. The licence still has conditions. |
| **Free access** | Useful material can be viewed or used without payment. Reuse rights vary. |
| **Free account** | Core access is free, but registration may be required. Protect student privacy and use board-approved accounts. |
| **Mixed** | Free and paid material appear together, or some features require payment. Filter carefully. |

Teacher review is required for public marketplaces, community galleries, comments, advertising, external downloads, and age-appropriate content. Machine-specific safety instruction and operating procedures follow school board guidelines and the course information provided by the teacher; students in Mr. Andrade's classes use Google Classroom for that material.

## Find ideas and understand products

Use these sources to identify needs, compare existing solutions, study mechanisms, and read build evidence. They are starting points for investigation, not answer banks.

| Resource | Best use | Access and checks |
|---|---|---|
| [Instructables](https://www.instructables.com/) | Build sequences, materials, tests, and maker documentation | Free access. Quality and licences vary by project. |
| [Hackaday.io Projects](https://hackaday.io/projects) | Open hardware, electronics, mechanisms, and prototypes | Free access. Check each project's files and licence. |
| [Arduino Project Hub](https://projecthub.arduino.cc/) | Documented physical-computing projects | Free access. Some builds require purchased parts or accounts. |
| [Adafruit Learning System](https://learn.adafruit.com/) | Detailed electronics, fabrication, coding, and wearable guides | Free access. Product links are commercial. |
| [SparkFun Learn](https://learn.sparkfun.com/) | Electronics tutorials, hookup guides, and classroom ideas | Free access. Confirm hardware versions. |
| [Raspberry Pi Projects](https://projects.raspberrypi.org/) | Guided computing and physical-computing projects | Free access. Hardware may be required. |
| [micro:bit Projects](https://microbit.org/projects/) | Short classroom coding and invention projects | Free access. Check local account and device policies. |
| [iFixit](https://www.ifixit.com/) | Teardowns, repair sequences, fasteners, and serviceability | Free access. Device-specific hazards still apply. |
| [Google Patents](https://patents.google.com/) | Product history, mechanisms, drawings, and claims | Free access. A patent drawing is not permission to copy a protected invention. |
| [Etsy](https://www.etsy.com/ca/search?q=tool%20holder) | Commercial precedents, product language, and user-review themes | Mixed marketplace. Analyze, do not copy sellers' work. |
| [Glowforge Catalog](https://glowforge.com/b/catalog) | Laser-cut product categories, layers, and construction ideas | Mixed. Visibility does not grant file or reproduction rights. |
| [Smithsonian Learning Lab](https://learninglab.si.edu/) | Museum objects, collections, and classroom investigations | Free access. Check rights on each item. |
| [OER Commons](https://www.oercommons.org/) | Open educational lessons and project resources | Free access. Check the licence on each resource. |

Use the [N.I.C.E. Design Process](../../01-nice-design-process/index.qmd) to turn investigation into criteria, alternatives, tests, and revisions. The [Good Idea, Better Product challenge](../../03-laser-cutting/resources/reverse-engineer-improve.qmd) provides a complete reverse-engineering assignment.

## Inclusive design, ergonomics, and accessibility

| Resource | Best use | Access and checks |
|---|---|---|
| [Cambridge Inclusive Design](https://www-edc.eng.cam.ac.uk/research/inclusive-design) | Designing for a range of capabilities and reducing exclusion | Free access to research and tools. |
| [Microsoft Inclusive Design guidebook](https://inclusive.microsoft.design/tools-and-activities/Inclusive101Guidebook.pdf) | Activities for recognizing exclusion and designing with people | Free PDF. Cite the source; do not treat personas as substitutes for real users. |
| [W3C Web Accessibility Initiative](https://www.w3.org/WAI/fundamentals/) | Accessibility principles that transfer to digital and physical communication | Free access. Use current W3C guidance. |
| [WebAIM Contrast Checker](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/) | Testing text and background colour contrast | Free access. Contrast is one accessibility check, not the whole experience. |
| [Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety: Ergonomics](https://www.ccohs.ca/oshanswers/ergonomics/) | Workstation, reach, posture, repetition, and task-design background | Free access. Apply local school and workplace requirements. |
| [The Centre for Excellence in Universal Design](https://universaldesign.ie/about-universal-design) | Universal-design principles and guidance | Free access. Adapt to the actual user and setting. |

## Downloadable 3D models and scans

Downloaded models can support comparison, remixing where permitted, museum study, or a component that would be wasteful to redraw. They should not replace original modelling in an assignment designed to assess CAD skill.

| Resource | Best use | Access and checks |
|---|---|---|
| [Printables](https://www.printables.com/) | Printable models, makes, comments, and remixes | Mixed community library. Check each licence and model history. |
| [Thingiverse](https://www.thingiverse.com/) | Large community model library | Free access. Licence, quality, and completeness vary. |
| [MakerWorld](https://makerworld.com/) | Models, profiles, makes, and print feedback | Mixed community library. Account may be required for some actions. |
| [Thangs free-model search](https://thangs.com/digital/search/free?scope=thangs&view=list) | Cross-library model discovery and geometric search | Mixed. A free filter does not replace checking the source licence. |
| [Sketchfab downloadable models](https://sketchfab.com/search?features=downloadable&type=models) | Rotating, inspecting, and downloading permitted 3D work | Mixed. Check each licence, attribution, and download format. |
| [GrabCAD Community Library](https://grabcad.com/library) | Mechanical CAD references and assemblies | Free account. Verify contributor rights, scale, and engineering suitability. |
| [NASA 3D Resources](https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/) | Spacecraft, terrain, and science models | Free downloads subject to NASA media-use guidelines. |
| [Smithsonian Open Access](https://www.si.edu/OpenAccess) | Museum scans, images, and 3D objects | Open access where marked. Check the record and usage guidance. |
| [NIH 3D](https://3d.nih.gov/) | Biomedical and scientific 3D models | Free access. Check each record; models are not automatically suitable for medical use. |
| [Scan the World](https://www.myminifactory.com/scantheworld/) | Cultural-heritage 3D scans | Mixed platform. Check the object's licence and cultural context. |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Online examples are not operating procedures

Online feeds, speeds, toolpaths, printer profiles, laser settings, electrical circuits, and material claims are examples, not universal instructions. Machine-specific safety instruction, operating procedures, assessments, and authorization are kept outside this public website. Follow your school board's safety guidelines and the course information provided by your teacher. Students in Mr. Andrade's classes can find that information in Google Classroom. Treat online values as hypotheses: simulate where appropriate, measure, make a controlled test, and investigate unexpected evidence.
:::

## A simple student source record

For every external reference, save:

1. creator or organization;
2. page, product, project, or file title;
3. direct URL and access date;
4. access label and stated licence;
5. what you learned from it;
6. what you reused, adapted, or deliberately changed;
7. what you verified through measurement, testing, or another source.

Do not submit a folder of links as research. Turn sources into evidence, criteria, alternatives, decisions, tests, and an original result.
